From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Access controls landing plan & escalation — engineering responses

Hi Marissa / Monica — quick answers for Catalyst so you can close the loop: 

1) Custom attribute mapping: We do not map arbitrary SCIM attributes directly into RBAC. Current pattern: SCIM creates users and core attributes (userName, emails, name, active), and we evaluate group assignment via a rule engine that can consume a mapped claim (SAML) or call a post-provisioning webhook. For "employeeType" we recommend either: a) include it as a SAML attribute so our rule engine assigns groups on SAML assertion, or b) set up a small post-provisioning webhook (we provide a sample) that maps the attribute to a group. I'll attach the webhook sample and a short snippet showing how to enable SAML -> group rules.

2) SCIM semantics: Confirmed — our SCIM implements PATCH for partial updates and supports DELETE for deprovisioning. The provisioning service returns 200/204 on success and 4xx/5xx with a body on failures. We expose retry with exponential backoff for transient 5xx; the default is 3 retries over ~30s. We log failures to the account trace and surface them in the Console under Provisioning -> Logs.

3) IP allowlist propagation: Authorizing CIDR in the Console pushes a network policy to the staging edge within ~5-7 minutes (typical). No BGP overlap detected with the sample list (quick check) — no conflicts. If they want a signed NOC confirmation I can generate one.

I'll paste the sample webhook (short) below and attach the file to the ticket you send.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference
